stem: Which X-ray finding is characteristic of developmental dysplasia of the hip in a child older than 6 months?

options.text: A larger femoral head ossification centre
A steeper acetabular roof with lateral displacement of the femoral head
Medial displacement of the femoral head

explanation: A steeper acetabular roof with lateral displacement of the femoral head is characteristic of developmental dysplasia of the hip on X-ray in an older infant. The socket is more vertical and the femoral head sits further from the acetabular centre.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because developmental dysplasia of the hip is associated with a steeper, not flattened, acetabular roof.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the affected femoral head ossification centre is typically delayed or smaller, not larger.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because a steeper acetabular roof and lateral displacement of the femoral head are classic X-ray features of developmental dysplasia of the hip.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because amniotic fluid markers are prenatal findings and are not seen on a postnatal hip X-ray.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the femoral head is displaced laterally in developmental dysplasia of the hip, not medially.

source.hint: Look for descriptions of the angle of the hip socket and the position of the femur.
